A0227.title: Teleoperation Channel Encryption & Authentication
A0227.definition: End-to-end encryption, mutual certificate authentication, command-sequence anti-replay, and latency-anomaly detection on robot teleoperation (teleop) control channels to prevent hijacking, replay, or injection.
A0227.description: Teleoperation channel encryption and authentication targets hijacking risks in remote control links for humanoid robots, surgical robots, and hazardous-operation robots, establishing a four-layer defense. First, end-to-end encryption ensures control commands are transmitted in ciphertext throughout, preventing man-in-the-middle eavesdropping and tampering. Second, mutual certificate authentication requires both the operator side and the robot side to verify each other's certificates, blocking unauthorized access to the channel. Third, command sequence numbers and timestamps attach a monotonically increasing sequence number to each command, with the receiver validating freshness to resist action replay. Fourth, latency anomaly detection addresses the delay sensitivity of teleoperation; injecting abnormal delays can disrupt the stability of fine operations, and detecting delay jitter enables identification of delay injection attacks. This measure is a core defense direction following incidents such as the Raven II surgical robot hijacking, and together with A0118 (certificate-based device authentication) and A0150 (OTA channel encryption and integrity protection) belongs to the communication security framework, with this measure specialized for the low-latency and anti-replay requirements of real-time control channels.
A0227.limitation: Encryption and authentication introduce additional communication latency, affecting the real-time performance of fine teleoperation (e.g., remote surgery). Certificate and key management is complex; lost devices or personnel changes require timely revocation. It cannot defend against internal attackers who already possess valid credentials. Latency detection may produce false positives under normal network fluctuations.
